To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a grammar form is complete if and only if it satisfies certain expansion conditions and that the expansion spectrum can be determined in polynomial time.

the set of complete grammar forms is a proper subset of the set of complete interpretations, that the set of linear complete grammar forms is equal to the set of linear interpretations, that the sets of complete and linear interpretations are both recursively enumerable, that the set C of complete interpretations is not recursive and that the set of noncomplete interpretations is recursively enumerable, while the set of complete noninterpretations is not recursively enumerable.

the class of complete grammar forms is precisely the class of grammar forms which have a non-empty intersection with the class of EOL forms, and that this intersection class is precisely the class whose members are all those forms which are generated by a super normal form grammar.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the following problem: Given a context-free grammar G = (V,C, P, S) and a finite set of productions Q, decide whether Q is a complete expansion spectrum for G. In Section 3 we will see that the problem is decidable.
the following question: For a given grammar form F, is there an interpretation of F which is complete?
a characterization of complete grammar form, a notion which is a refinement of the concept of a complete context-free grammar.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the grammar form (V, C,P, S) is complete iff the following conditions are satisfied: (i) the grammar form is linear, (ii) the grammar form has no nonterminals, (iii) the grammar form generates a context-free language, (iv) the grammar form does not generate any non-context-free language.
a grammar form G is complete if and only if for all nonterminals X, Y, Z E V, there exist words w, u E C* and a production of the form Xw -+ YZu.
a grammar form is complete iff it is linear complete and has the super normal form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that all grammar forms are equivalent in their power to generate context-free languages, but that there is a wide variety of different forms, and that the study of the different classes of forms is of considerable mathematical interest in its own right.

the study of grammar forms and interpretations has led to the development of a powerful and flexible tool for the study of context-free languages, and in particular, for the study of parsing and the design of parsing algorithms.
we have shown that the notion of completeness of grammar forms is a very powerful tool to study context-free grammars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the grammar forms are a natural class of grammars that is closed under many operations, such as union, intersection, and concatenation.
we can now use a grammar to describe a context-free language and then use the context-free language to describe the grammar.
the notion of completeness for grammar forms is a natural and useful one, and that it is decidable.
